Chapter 9: The Joy of God in Suffering and Sacrifice.
There’s a kind of beauty that only shows up in the hardest places. Maybe you’ve seen it—a nurse gently holding a trembling hand, a friend quietly sitting next to a hospital bed, or a family choosing hope even as they face heartbreaking loss.
These moments are filled with pain, but there’s also this strange, unexpected joy that somehow shines through. In a way that’s hard to wrap your mind around, God actually finds pleasure—even in suffering and sacrifice.
Now, let’s be honest—this is probably the hardest part of the story to accept. Suffering just feels so pointless, so unfair. Sometimes, it even seems cruel. You might wonder, how could any good possibly come from pain? But here’s the thing: the story of God’s pleasure isn’t about pretending suffering doesn’t exist, or trying to escape it. It’s about presence. It’s about purpose. And it’s about a hope that hangs on, even when everything hurts.
Picture this: someone you know faces a deep loss. Yet, in the middle of it, they choose to forgive, to love, to trust—despite the pain. Those choices don’t come easy. There are tears, tough questions, and moments filled with doubt. But there’s also a deep connection, a kind of grace that just can’t be explained.
Most people walk right past this kind of beauty. But God doesn’t. His joy isn’t in the suffering itself, but in the love that keeps going, the faith that refuses to give up, the hope that just won’t die. It’s in those places of suffering where God’s presence feels most real, where His comfort is what you cling to, and where His strength is almost tangible.
At some point, it becomes clear: sacrifice isn’t really about losing for the sake of loss. It’s about love. When someone gives up comfort, security, or even their own dreams for someone else, something beautiful happens. God delights in these moments of self-giving—in the willingness to put someone else first, even when it costs you.
And that changes the way we see suffering and sacrifice. They’re not meaningless. They’re not wasted. Instead, they become places where God’s joy shows up in ways you never expected. So, worship? It turns into an act of trust—a way of saying, “God, I believe you’re good, even when life is hard.”
